Topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Probability

Target audience: University students (Introductory Statistics/Data Science)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: Conditional Probability & Visual Logic

Lecture lines:
Conditional probability: P(A|B) narrows our universe.
Consider our total sample space, S.
Subset B acts as our new reality.
The intersection represents occurrences of A given B.
Example: Orange animal reduces our animal cage set.

Planned animations:
Fade in text 'P(A|B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B)' in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight intersection area in light blue #ADD8E6 within Venn diagram.
Animate shrinking 'B' circle to demonstrate P(B) as denominator.
Flash P(A ∩ B) label #FFFFE0 to emphasize numerator.
Fade in 'Evidence changes our belief' text #F0F8FF.

Section: section_2 — Independence: The 'No Influence' Condition

Lecture lines:
Independence: Knowing B provides zero info about A.
Mathematically, this means P(A|B) equals P(A).
Imagine a coin flip and a spinning wheel.

Planned animations:
Fade in two independent sets A and B as separate circles.
Display equation 'P(A|B) = P(A)' in white #FFFFFF.
Animate B moving without changing A's size to show independence.

Section: section_3 — Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversing Evidence

Lecture lines:
Bayes' Theorem: Reversing the logic of evidence.
We calculate P(A|B) using the likelihood.
It connects P(B|A) back to our original prior.
This updates our belief with new data.
Crucial for real-world smart device accuracy.

Planned animations:
Display 'P(A|B) = P(B|A) * P(A) / P(B)' in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight P(B|A) term in yellow #FFFF00 for emphasis.
Show transition from prior to posterior using an arrow #FFFFFF.
Flash P(B) label #FFC0CB to indicate normalization factor.
Fade in visual balance scale icon comparing prior and posterior.

Section: section_4 — Synthesis & Real-world Application

Lecture lines:
Synthesizing: Prior, Evidence, and Posterior probability.
Bayes' updates certainty in the face of uncertainty.
Testing example: Prior prevalence informs posterior diagnosis.

Planned animations:
Fade in text 'Medical Diagnosis Example' in white #FFFFFF.
Display test sensitivity and false positive rates.
Animate final probability calculation with bold result #00FF00.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
